root_cause.text: The PCI SR-IOV code in `drivers/pci/iov.c` incorrectly added `pci_rescan_remove_lock` around `sriov_add_vfs()`/`sriov_del_vfs()`, causing `sriov_disable()` to recursively reacquire the same lock when VF removal runs during `pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked()`.
root_cause.evidence: The reverted patch removes `pci_lock_rescan_remove()`/`pci_unlock_rescan_remove()` from `sriov_add_vfs()` and `sriov_del_vfs()`, and the commit message explicitly says commit `05703271c3cd` "causes a deadlock by recursively taking pci_rescan_remove_lock when sriov_del_vfs() is called as part of pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device()," with the trace showing the lock already held in `pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked()` and reacquired in `sriov_disable()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The PCI SR-IOV code in `drivers/pci/iov.c` incorrectly added `pci_rescan_remove_lock` around `sriov_add_vfs()`/`sriov_del_vfs()`, causing `sriov_disable()` to recursively reacquire the same lock when VF removal runs during `pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked()`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The reverted patch removes `pci_lock_rescan_remove()`/`pci_unlock_rescan_remove()` from `sriov_add_vfs()` and `sriov_del_vfs()`, and the commit message explicitly says commit `05703271c3cd` "causes a deadlock by recursively taking pci_rescan_remove_lock when sriov_del_vfs() is called as part of pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device()," with the trace showing the lock already held in `pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked()` and reacquired in `sriov_disable()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant or incorrect PCI rescan/remove locking from sriov_add_vfs() so VF creation and rollback use the proper synchronization context.
intent_record.what: The calls to pci_lock_rescan_remove() before the VF creation loop and pci_unlock_rescan_remove() on both the success and failure paths were removed from sriov_add_vfs(), while the loop adding virtual functions and the rollback loop removing already-added virtual functions remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, sriov_add_vfs() no longer acquires or releases the PCI rescan/remove lock around virtual function addition and rollback. This changes synchronization behavior by avoiding that lock in this function, likely relying on locking being handled elsewhere and preventing incorrect or redundant lock usage during VF creation or cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant rescan/remove locking from sriov_del_vfs() so VF removal uses the correct synchronization behavior.
intent_record.what: The change removes the calls to pci_lock_rescan_remove() before the loop and pci_unlock_rescan_remove() after the loop in sriov_del_vfs(), leaving only the iteration that calls pci_iov_remove_virtfn(dev, i) for each VF.
intent_record.how: At runtime, sriov_del_vfs() no longer acquires and releases the PCI rescan/remove lock around virtual function removal, so VF deletion now relies on locking handled elsewhere or avoids redundant locking that could cause incorrect synchronization behavior such as lock imbalance or deadlock.

grouping_result.intent: Remove redundant rescan/remove locking from sriov_del_vfs() so VF removal uses the correct synchronization behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove redundant PCI rescan/remove locking from SR-IOV VF add/remove paths so VF lifecycle operations rely on the correct synchronization context.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly remove the incorrect/redundant pci_rescan_remove_lock usage around sriov_add_vfs()/sriov_del_vfs(), which is the stated root cause of the recursive lock reacquisition in sriov_disable().

candidates.rationale: This added the PCI rescan/remove lock around sriov_add_vfs(), matching the root cause that SR-IOV VF lifecycle paths incorrectly took this lock and could conflict with the proper synchronization context.

This is the most direct cause of the bug in VF removal: sriov_del_vfs() acquired pci_rescan_remove_lock even though VF removal can run under pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked(), leading to recursive reacquisition in sriov_disable().

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement incorrectly acquires the PCI rescan/remove lock in the VF removal path. When sriov_disable() triggers VF removal under pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked(), the same lock is already held, so this causes recursive lock reacquisition and the vulnerability.

This statement incorrectly acquires the PCI rescan/remove lock in the VF creation/rollback path. The fix intent identifies this locking as redundant or incorrect synchronization around sriov_add_vfs(), consistent with the root cause that SR-IOV VF lifecycle paths should not take this lock here.

commit 05703271c3cdcc0f2a8cf6ebdc45892b8ca83520
Author: Niklas Schnelle <schnelle@linux.ibm.com>
Date:   Tue Aug 26 10:52:08 2025 +0200

    PCI/IOV: Add PCI rescan-remove locking when enabling/disabling SR-IOV
    
    Before disabling SR-IOV via config space accesses to the parent PF,
    sriov_disable() first removes the PCI devices representing the VFs.
    
    Since commit 9d16947b7583 ("PCI: Add global pci_lock_rescan_remove()")
    such removal operations are serialized against concurren
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact locking added around the SR-IOV VF add/remove helpers, which is the logic described in the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present in this commit: `sriov_add_vfs()` now does `pci_lock_rescan_remove();` before the loop calling `pci_iov_add_virtfn(dev, i);` and `pci_unlock_rescan_remove();` afterward, and `sriov_del_vfs()` now does `pci_lock_rescan_remove();` before the loop calling `pci_iov_remove_virtfn(dev, i);` and unlocks afterward. Per the root cause, adding `pci_rescan_remove_lock` around `sriov_add_vfs()`/`sriov_del_vfs()` is exactly the incorrect change, because VF removal during `sriov_disable()` can later recurse into `pci_stop_and_remove_bus_device_locked()` and try to reacquire the same lock. Therefore this commit contains the vulnerable construct. It does not contain the fix, because the fix would remove or restructure this locking to avoid recursive reacquisition; instead, this commit is the one introducing the locking.

Author: Sebastian Ott <sebott@linux.ibm.com>
Date:   Fri Dec 21 15:14:18 2018 +0100

    PCI/IOV: Factor out sriov_add_vfs()
    
    Provide sriov_add_vfs() as a wrapper to scan for VFs that cleans up after
    itself.  This is just a code simplification.  No functional change.
    
    Signed-off-by: Sebastian Ott <sebott@linux.ibm.com>
    Signed-off-by: Bjorn Helgaas <bhelgaas@google.com>
    Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>

diff --
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the complete newly introduced helper functions and the relevant call sites in `sriov_enable()` and `sriov_disable()`. The root cause described is the incorrect addition of `pci_rescan_remove_lock` around `sriov_add_vfs()` / `sriov_del_vfs()`, which would cause recursive lock reacquisition during VF removal. In this commit, `sriov_add_vfs()` is only a simple wrapper: `for (i = 0; i < num_vfs; i++) { rc = pci_iov_add_virtfn(dev, i); ... }` with cleanup via `pci_iov_remove_virtfn(dev, i)`. Likewise, `sriov_del_vfs()` only does `for (i = 0; i < iov->num_VFs; i++) pci_iov_remove_virtfn(dev, i);`. There is no `pci_rescan_remove_lock` or corresponding unlock anywhere in the shown code, so the vulnerable construct is absent. Because the bug is specifically about adding that lock around these helpers, this commit does not itself contain the bug. At the same time, the later fix for that bug is also not present here, because there is no lock handling to correct or remove; this commit is merely the refactoring that introduces the helper wrappers.
